# server Specification

## Purpose

The standalone central-server backend (`se3-server`) plus bundled web frontend, its multi-tenant identity/auth/persistence model, and the owner-scoped REST/WebSocket surfaces.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Server Modules

`src/se3/server/` is the standalone package for the central-server backend plus its bundled web frontend; it isolates the heavy web dependencies via `pyproject.toml` optional-dependencies (`se3[server]`) and is launched through the separate console_scripts entry point `se3-server` — not built as a subcommand of the core `se3`. New server submodules must be registered in this spec.

- `app.py` — the FastAPI application entry point: `create_app` assembles the routes, `run` / `main` start it via `uvicorn` (the `uvicorn.run` call is given `ws_max_size=protocol.MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` so the server's inbound frame limit is lifted off uvicorn's 16 MiB default to the shared protocol cap — this is the limit that was silently dropping oversized daemon→server `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames and surfacing as a `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` 504) and parse `--host` / `--port` / `--version` (`--version` is only a completeness supplement to the argparse help text; the real interception happens in `src/se3/server/__init__.py:main` before FastAPI / uvicorn are imported, with output format `se3-server version {__version__}` aligned with the core `se3 version`); it provides a REST API (machine / flow queries, remotely publishing new tasks, answering pending call/interjection) and mounts `static/` at `/`; `create_app` wires the multi-tenant auth/identity layer **fail-closed**: it constructs the `Store` (sqlite, from `server.db_path`), the `SessionStore`, the `LoginRateLimiter`, the `IdentityService`, and the `ProviderChain` (via `build_provider_chain`, raising `AuthNotConfigured` and refusing to start when no usable provider is configured), and every `/api/*` data route carries `Depends(require_owner)` so an unauthenticated request is rejected with 401; the resolved `OwnerIdentity` is mapped to an owner scope (`_scope_for`) and threaded into the `ServerState` query methods so all machine / flow / history reads are owner-filtered, and `POST /api/flows` / `respond` / `interject` first verify the target machine / flow belongs to the current owner (a foreign target reads as 404), closing the prior identity-unaware remote-command-dispatch hole; `POST /api/flows` additionally accepts an optional `from_issue_id` parameter (composable with the existing `discover` parameter): when supplied, the server resolves the issue owner-scoped (reusing `ServerState.get_issue_by_id(..., owner=...)`, so an issue on a machine/project outside the caller's owner scope — or an unknown id — reads as 404) to obtain the authoritative target machine/project, then threads `from_issue_id` through `make_spawn_flow` to the owning daemon so the spawned flow is started from that issue (the request's `task_description` being ignored in that case); the auth surface adds `POST /api/auth/login` (username+password → session cookie), `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` (the current `OwnerIdentity`), and `POST /api/auth/breakglass` (consume a one-time break-glass token → the single stable break-glass admin owner, lazily created via `_ensure_breakglass_admin`); the owner self-service surface adds `POST /api/daemon-keys` (mint a daemon key bound to the current owner, returning the plaintext once), `GET /api/daemon-keys` (list the owner's key metadata), and `DELETE /api/daemon-keys/{key_id}` (revoke); and the admin-gated user-management surface — every route independently enforcing `Depends(require_owner)` + an `is_admin` check (a non-admin caller is rejected 403, before any existence check so the surface leaks nothing) via a shared `create_app`-local `_require_admin` guard, never relying on the frontend hiding the entry — comprises `POST /api/users` (create / invite a local user), `GET /api/users` (list manageable owners as a strict field whitelist — `owner_id` / `display_name` / `is_admin` / `created_at` / identity `provider` / a `can_reset_password` flag — never returning password or daemon-key hashes or any other sensitive field, with the break-glass owner filtered out server-side by reverse-resolving its reserved `(BREAKGLASS_PROVIDER, …)` binding), `DELETE /api/users/{owner_id}` (delete a user, cascading the cleanup of its bindings / credentials / daemon keys via `store.delete_owner` under `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign keys), `POST /api/users/{owner_id}/password` (reset password — only for `local`-provider owners, reusing `crypto.hash_password` + `store.set_password` with the plaintext hashed off the event loop and never logged; an OIDC / proxy-header owner is refused), and `POST /api/users/{owner_id}/admin` (toggle the `is_admin` flag, reusing the new `store.set_admin`); these mutating routes enforce the non-reversible authorization invariants server-side — the caller may not delete or demote itself, the system's last non-break-glass admin may not be deleted or demoted (the last-admin count-and-write is performed atomically inside `store.delete_owner_guarded` / `store.set_admin_guarded` under a single held lock to close the read-then-write TOCTOU race), the break-glass owner may not be deleted / demoted / password-reset (reading as 404), and an unknown / reserved `owner_id` reads as 404; it includes the history query endpoints `GET /api/history` (the historical session list) and `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` (a session's step conversation records): on every request, `GET /api/history` first broadcasts `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST` to all connected daemons via `broadcast_index_refresh`, waits with a bound for each daemon to force-re-push its latest index (registering/deregistering waiters via `IndexRefreshRegistry`), then aggregates and returns, so that "entering the history list fetches the latest history" without the user manually hard-refreshing; when there is no connected daemon or the wait times out, it robustly degrades to returning the currently cached index (without blocking and without error); `GET /api/history/{flow_id}`, on a cache miss, sends `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` to the corresponding daemon and waits for the data to return, with the wait bound controlled by the module-level constant `HISTORY_PULL_TIMEOUT` (currently `30.0` seconds), whose value must be large enough to cover the real disk-read time of a daemon's cold-start first pull of a large session containing several MB of jsonl — even though the daemon already offloads the read to a worker thread as required by `client.py` in *Daemon Modules*, the disk read itself still has appreciable latency, and too narrow a window would return 504 while the daemon is healthy but still reading; `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` additionally accepts an optional `after` query parameter carrying an **opaque progress token** the client echoes on a WebSocket-reconnect re-fetch so the server can return only the records that accrued during the outage instead of the whole bundle: every response carries a `delivery` field (`"delta"` or `"full"`) and a fresh `progress` token, the token is produced and validated inside `state.py` (see `ServerState`), and the route serves a delta **only** on a cache hit whose bundle still pins the echoed token — every unsafe case (a missing / malformed / tampered token, a generation mismatch from a `mode: full` cache replacement, a machine / owner change, or a cache miss that pulls fresh records from the daemon) falls back to returning the full record list with `delivery: "full"` and a new token; the existing owner / ownership validation (`require_owner`, `find_machine_for_history_flow`) and the cache-miss daemon-pull semantics are unchanged by the incremental path; it adds the `POST /api/flows/{flow_id}/interject` endpoint, wrapping the mid-flight interjection typed in the web console via `make_interject_flow` into `MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW` and dispatching it to the daemon that owns the flow (fire-and-forget dispatch, returns `202`); it provides the `GET /api/version` endpoint returning `{"version": __version__}`, for the frontend to render the current se3 version number in the top bar, with the version read from the single source `se3.__version__`; it adds the **flow resume** endpoint `POST /api/flows/{flow_id}/resume`, which validates (owner-scoped) that the target flow is **directly resumable** — owned by the caller, in a `FAILED` or `PAUSED` status (`ServerState.is_flow_resumable` / `RESUMABLE_STATUSES`), not archived/history-only, and on a currently-connected machine — and on success dispatches a `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` carrying `resume_flow_id` to the owning daemon (returning `202`), mapping a non-resumable / cross-owner / unknown flow to `404`; and it adds the **owner-scoped issue-management REST surface** mirroring each daemon's on-disk issues from the `STATUS_UPDATE` snapshot: `GET /api/issues` (list across the owner's machines, optionally filtered by `machine_id` / `project_root` / `include_closed` / `source` / `type`), `GET /api/issues/{issue_id}` (single issue), `POST /api/issues` (create — `description` required, other fields optional, written with `source="human"`), `PATCH /api/issues/{issue_id}` (edit), `POST /api/issues/{issue_id}/close` (with optional `reason`), and `POST /api/issues/{issue_id}/reopen`. The four write routes resolve the owning machine from the issue mirror, dispatch a `protocol.make_issue_command` (`create` / `edit` / `close` / `reopen`) to that daemon, and await the correlated `MSG_ISSUE_RESULT` via an `IssueCommandRegistry` (bounded by the short per-operation `ISSUE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, currently `10.0` seconds). On an ack timeout the route MUST NOT immediately report failure: because the daemon may already have persisted the issue with only the ack delayed (e.g. behind a heavy daemon-side snapshot racing the periodic pushes), `_send_issue_command` falls back to a bounded **reconcile** window (`_reconcile_issue_command`, bounded by `ISSUE_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT`, currently `15.0` seconds, polling every `ISSUE_RECONCILE_POLL_INTERVAL`, currently `0.5` seconds) that checks the operation's expected post-condition against the in-memory issue mirror (refreshed by `STATUS_UPDATE`): `create` looks for a new `source="human"` issue under the target `project_root` whose id is absent from the pre-send baseline id set (snapshotted before dispatch, since the daemon — not the server — allocates the new id), while `edit` / `close` / `reopen` key off the known `target_issue_id` and confirm the expected field updates / a no-longer-open(in-progress) status / a reopened-open status respectively. If reconcile observes the post-condition it corrects the result to success (returning the affected `issue_id` with `reconciled=True`) so the front end sees a created/succeeded outcome instead of a spurious red failure for an issue that already landed on disk; only if the reconcile window also elapses with the change still absent does the route return failure. The reconcile fallback triggers **only** on the ack `TimeoutError`, so it never masks a genuine daemon-reported failure (an explicit `ok=false` ack still surfaces as failure). The reconcile path reuses the existing in-memory mirror (`state.get_issues` / `state.get_issue_by_id`) and adds no server-side disk read, preserving the architecture boundary that the daemon is the only issue-persistence edge. Like the other data routes every issue route carries `Depends(require_owner)` and only ever sees issues on the caller's own machines (a foreign machine/issue reads as `404`)
- `ws.py` — the WebSocket endpoint: manages the daemon connection pool (connect / disconnect / heartbeat) and the frontend `UiHub` broadcast channel, routing protocol messages (daemon→server status reports, server→daemon command dispatch). For the multi-tenant control plane, the daemon `/ws` HELLO is authenticated fail-closed: the server reads the HELLO `key`, resolves it via `IdentityService.resolve_owner_for_key(key) → owner_id`, binds the machine to that owner (`bind_machine`, setting `MachineRecord.owner_id`), and on a missing / invalid key (or a malformed / non-HELLO opening frame, or a missing `machine_id`) answers `WELCOME(accepted=false, reason=...)` and closes the socket without entering the receive loop. The frontend `/ws/ui` channel is owner-scoped: each UI client is registered in `UiHub` with the `owner_id` it authenticated as (resolved via `require_owner`; an unresolved owner fail-closes the socket), and every push is filtered to that owner's trust domain — `UiHub` precomputes one payload per distinct owner so a client never sees another owner's machines / flows / history; it also routes history messages (`MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` / `MSG_HISTORY_DATA`) by writing them into `ServerState` and broadcasting to `/ws/ui`; and it provides `IndexRefreshRegistry` (registering in-flight index re-push waits by `machine_id`, isomorphic to `HistoryRequestRegistry` but keyed by machine rather than flow) and the `broadcast_index_refresh` helper (dispatching `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST` to each online daemon and registering the corresponding future); upon receiving a daemon's `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX`, besides updating the cache it also resolves the corresponding waiter, so that `GET /api/history` syncs to each daemon's re-pushed latest index before aggregating; and it routes a daemon's `MSG_ISSUE_RESULT` by resolving the matching `IssueCommandRegistry` waiter keyed by `request_id`, so the awaiting issue REST handler can return the daemon's `ok` / `error` acknowledgment; and it routes a daemon's `MSG_SPAWN_FAILED` — sent when a spawn/init genuinely fails on the daemon host (e.g. an `ensure_se3_project` init failure, where `client._handle_spawn` no longer silently returns) — by translating it into a `UI_EVENT_SPAWN_FAILED` frame (carrying the originating `machine_id` / `project_root` / `error` plus, when present, `task_description` / `from_issue_id` / `resume_flow_id`) and broadcasting it to that owner's `/ws/ui` clients, so the web console flips the just-published task from a "published" state to a visible error rather than leaving it silently stuck
- `state.py` — `ServerState`, the in-memory multi-machine / multi-flow aggregated state store. Machine / flow / history live state stays in memory and is rebuilt from daemon reconnects — it is deliberately NOT written to the new sqlite persistence layer (which holds only the identity facts that cannot be reconstructed; see `persistence.py`). `MachineRecord` now also carries an `owner_id` (the trust domain the machine's daemon authenticated as, set when the HELLO key resolves; see `ws.py` / `identity.py`) alongside `project_roots: List[str]`; the machine / flow / history query methods take an `owner` scope argument and filter the returned view so a caller only ever sees machines / flows / history belonging to its own `owner_id`, with a cross-owner machine or flow reading as not-found (404). `update_status` reads `project_roots` from the daemon snapshot and saves it, and `/api/machines` returns this field in the `include_flows=False` overview for frontend linkage; the store additionally caches the historical session index and the already-pulled historical data (purely as in-memory relay / cache, not persisted to disk). Each cached history bundle also carries an in-memory `generation` lifecycle id (handed out fresh whenever the bundle is first built or replaced by a `mode: full` push, kept stable across ordinary `append` pushes). **Old-format (generation-less) bundle backward compatibility:** a bundle produced before the `generation` field existed is back-filled with a stable positive `generation` on first contact (via a shared `_ensure_generation` helper applied in both `get_history` and `get_history_snapshot`, and in the `append`-extend path so an append on a legacy bundle also carries a `generation`), so a generation-less old session participates in token validation as a first-class value and is served via the **delta** path instead of being forced into a permanent full-reload fallback (the prior bug: an old bundle's missing `generation` read as `0`, never matched a progress token's `generation` (≥1), and so always fell back to full). On a delta, the offset is clamped to `[0, total]`; any full fallback always returns the **complete** record set so the delivered records equal the on-disk jsonl in full regardless of delivery mode. `state.py` provides the `encode_progress` / `decode_progress` helpers that mint and validate the **opaque, HMAC-signed progress token** echoed by `GET /api/history/{flow_id}`'s `after` parameter, binding `(generation, offset, machine_id)` so a token issued before an append still validates while a token issued against a since-replaced bundle does not. The history-snapshot read method serves the delta tail and the full record list atomically under the same lock — it validates the echoed token against the current bundle and expected machine, returns the records after the token's `offset` with `delivery: "delta"` when the token still pins the bundle, and returns the full records with `delivery: "full"` (plus a new token) on every fallback (no token, stale / mismatched generation, machine / owner change, or cache miss); the token is content-free (it carries no record bodies) and signed so a client cannot forge or advance the offset and silently skip records. `update_status` also ingests the snapshot's `issues` list into a per-machine, per-`project_root` issue mirror (`_issues`), and `ServerState` exposes owner-scoped `get_issues(...)` (with `machine_id` / `project_root` / `include_closed` / `source` / `type_filter` filters) and `get_issue_by_id(...)` over that mirror, plus `is_flow_resumable(flow_id, owner=...)` which returns the `(machine_id, flow)` pair only when the flow is owner-visible and its status is in `RESUMABLE_STATUSES` (`{failed, paused}`) — the in-memory authority behind the issue REST surface and the `POST /api/flows/{id}/resume` gate; the issue mirror, like all machine/flow/history live state, is rebuilt from daemon snapshots and deliberately NOT persisted to sqlite
- `persistence.py` — the embedded-sqlite persistence layer: the project's **first** persistence layer (the codebase was previously pure-in-memory — `state.py` historically scoped DB out), introduced as the source of truth for facts that cannot be rebuilt by a daemon reconnecting. It defines the `Store` repository encapsulating all SQL behind a Postgres-swappable interface (callers never see SQL) over exactly five tables: `owners` (the opaque internal `owner_id` primary key + `display_name` + `is_admin`), `identity_bindings` (`(provider, external_id) → owner_id`, one owner may carry many bindings, one external identity maps to one owner), `local_credentials` (the argon2/bcrypt password hash keyed by `owner_id`), `daemon_keys` (issued daemon-key **hashes** bound to an owner), and `breakglass_tokens` (one-time admin break-glass token **hashes**). Beyond the existing `delete_owner` / `set_password` writes, the `Store` adds a `set_admin` update method (`UPDATE owners.is_admin`, returning whether the `owner_id` was hit, same `_lock` + commit + rowcount style as its siblings) backing the admin-toggle route, plus the guarded variants `delete_owner_guarded` / `set_admin_guarded` that perform the last-non-break-glass-admin count-check and the delete / demote write atomically under one held lock. Schema is tracked via `PRAGMA user_version` with an append-only migration list; WAL journal mode + per-thread connections make the single-file DB safe under the server's async + worker-thread access. The DB path comes from `server.db_path` (default `~/.se3/server.db`; `:memory:` for tests). Machine / flow live state is deliberately NOT stored here
- `crypto.py` — the credential-crypto helpers: slow password hashing (`hash_password` / `verify_password`, preferring argon2id via argon2-cffi and falling back to bcrypt), secure random token generation (daemon key / session id / break-glass token), `token_hash` (SHA-256 hashing for at-rest storage of keys/tokens), constant-time comparison (`hmac.compare_digest` / the argon2/bcrypt verifiers), and a redaction helper so credentials never leak into logs
- `identity.py` — the B-layer identity & authorization model, independent of the A-layer provider in use, sitting on top of `Store`: `IdentityService` provides `resolve_owner_for_key(key)` (hash the daemon key, look up its `owner_id`), the in-memory `machine_id → owner_id` index (`bind_machine` / `owner_of_machine` / `unbind_machine`, intentionally NOT persisted because it is live state rebuilt from daemon reconnects), and `link_identity_to_owner` — the cross-provider account-linking **trust gate** seam. 92	    clarification, a confirm gate) and is later resumed keeps being read
93	    incrementally rather than dropping out of the active set the moment it

95	    the enum value verbatim (e.g. ``"RUNNING"`` / ``"PAUSED"``).

102	#: ``se3.engine.models`` would execute ``se3.engine.__init__`` and drag the
103	#: whole engine (``llm_caller`` / ``state_machine`` / …) into the daemon's
104	#: import graph, against the daemon's deferred-import design. Used only as a
105	#: *soft* confidence signal by :func:`parse_step_type_from_step_id`; a name
106	#: that follows the file-name convention but is absent here still parses to its
107	#: middle segment, so a future step type drifting out of this set degrades to
108	#: best-effort rather than to a wrong answer.
109	_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES = frozenset(
110	    {
111	        "discovery",
112	        "analyze",
113	        "project_summary",
114	        "plan",
115	        "propose",
116	        "design",
117	        "plan_tasks",

131	def parse_step_type_from_step_id(stem: str) -> str:
132	    """Parse the authoritative step type out of a history jsonl file-name stem.
133	
134	    Real daemon chat-history files are named by the convention
135	    ``NN_<step_type>_<hash>(_Gk)`` (the file-name stem; ``NN`` is a two-digit
136	    sequence number, ``<hash>`` a hexadecimal id, and an optional ``_Gk`` group
137	    suffix is appended for DAG-grouped steps). The raw ``message`` records the
138	    daemon pushes carry *no* ``step_type`` field, so this parser recovers it
139	    deterministically from the stem instead of having the frontend guess.
140	
141	    The middle segment may itself contain underscores (e.g. ``version_analyze``),
142	    so the parser peels the known structural pieces — leading ``NN_`` sequence,
143	    trailing ``_G\\d+`` group suffix, trailing hexadecimal hash — and treats
144	    whatever remains as the step type. Examples::
145	
146	        01_discovery_975607bb      -> "discovery"
147	        13_version_analyze_def456  -> "version_analyze"
148	        05_implement_61605e42_G2   -> "implement"
149	
150	    The result is soft-validated against :data:`_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES`. A name that
151	    clearly follows the convention but whose type is not (yet) known still
152	    returns its parsed middle segment (self-describing, drift-tolerant). An
153	    old / non-conforming name with no sequence prefix and no hash tail (e.g.
154	    the legacy ``commit_summary``) gracefully falls back to the original stem
155	    rather than guessing.
156	
157	    This is a pure function: it never reads disk, has no side effects, and never
158	    raises — any unexpected input yields an empty string.
159	    """
160	    try:
161	        if not isinstance(stem, str):
162	            return ""
163	        original = stem.strip()
164	        if not original:
165	            return ""
166	
167	        # Defensive: if a physical / sidecar file name slipped through (e.g.
168	        # ``01_discovery_ab12.jsonl`` or
169	        # ``01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b``) instead of a logical
170	        # step id, reduce it to the logical id by stripping the ``.jsonl``
171	        # extension and any trailing ``.from-<branch>`` sidecar suffix first, so
172	        # callers that pass a raw name still parse the right step type.
173	        marker = original.find(".jsonl")
174	        if marker >= 0:
175	            original = original[:marker].strip()
176	            if not original:
177	                return ""
178	
179	        s = original
180	
181	        # 1. Strip a leading numeric sequence number ("NN_").
182	        without_seq = re.sub(r"^\d+_", "", s, count=1)
183	        seq_stripped = without_seq != s
184	        s = without_seq
185	
186	        # 2. Strip an optional trailing group suffix ("_G\\d+").
187	        without_group = re.sub(r"_G\d+$", "", s, count=1)
188	        group_stripped = without_group != s
189	        s = without_group
190	
191	        # 3. Strip a trailing hexadecimal hash segment, keeping the middle
192	        #    (which may itself contain underscores, e.g. "version_analyze").
193	        hash_stripped = False
194	        parts = s.split("_")
195	        if (
196	            len(parts) >= 2
197	            and parts[-1]
198	            and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]+", parts[-1])
199	        ):
200	            s = "_".join(parts[:-1])
201	            hash_stripped = True
202	
203	        candidate = s.strip("_")
204	
205	        # Soft-validate against the known step types (authoritative confidence).
206	        if candidate in _KNOWN_STEP_TYPES:
207	            return candidate
208	
209	        # Followed the naming convention (had a sequence / hash / group marker)
210	        # but the type is not in the known set: the parsed middle is still the
211	        # best self-describing answer, so future step types keep working.
212	        if candidate and (seq_stripped or hash_stripped or group_stripped):
213	            return candidate
214	
215	        # Old / non-conforming name (no NN prefix, no hash, e.g.
216	        # "commit_summary"): fall back to the original stem rather than guess.
217	        return original
218	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - parser must never raise
219	        return ""

225	#: TTL (seconds) for the cached :meth:`DaemonHistoryReader.build_index` result.
226	#: The daemon client's :meth:`~se3.daemon.client.DaemonClient._push_loop` calls
227	#: ``build_index`` every fast tick (1 s) via ``_push_history``.  On a machine
228	#: with a large history tree the full directory walk + JSON parse is expensive
229	#: enough to saturate the thread-pool workers and starve the event loop of CPU
230	#: (the same class of stall the aggregator's ``HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL`` fixed for
231	#: ``all_project_roots``).  Caching the index for a conservative window
232	#: collapses repeated identical rebuilds into one, while still reflecting new
233	#: flows within the window.

280	class FlowRead:
281	    """The result of one :func:`DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow` call.
282	
283	    Attributes:
284	        flow_id: The flow these records belong to.
285	        mode: :data:`~se3.daemon.protocol.HISTORY_MODE_FULL` for the initial
286	            batch (the requester had no cursor) or
287	            :data:`~se3.daemon.protocol.HISTORY_MODE_APPEND` for a delta.
288	        records: A list of ``{"step_id": str, "step_type": str, "message":
289	            dict}`` records, one per conversation line, ordered by step file
290	            then line. ``step_type`` is the authoritative type parsed from the
291	            jsonl file-name stem (see :func:`parse_step_type_from_step_id`); it
292	            is injected at the envelope level so the frontend never has to guess
293	            it, while ``message`` keeps its original bytes untouched.
294	        cursor: The updated per-step line cursor to send back on the next
295	            request to continue incrementally.
296	    """
297	
298	    flow_id: str
299	    mode: str
300	    records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
301	    cursor: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)

304	class DaemonHistoryReader:
305	    """Builds a history index and serves incremental per-flow conversation reads."""
306	
307	    def __init__(self, project_roots_provider: ProjectRootsProvider) -> None:
308	        """Create a reader.
309	
310	        Args:
311	            project_roots_provider: Zero-arg callable returning the project
312	                roots whose ``se3/history`` should be enumerated. Wiring this
313	                to the aggregator's ``project_roots`` keeps the history view in
314	                lock-step with the rest of the daemon's tracked roots.
315	        """
316	        self._provider = project_roots_provider
317	        # TTL cache for :meth:`build_index`.  The daemon client's push loop
318	        # calls ``build_index`` every fast tick (1 s); on a large history tree
319	        # the full directory walk + JSON parse is expensive enough to saturate
320	        # thread-pool workers.  Caching for a conservative window collapses
321	        # repeated identical rebuilds into one.
322	        self._index_cache: Optional[List[SessionMeta]] = None
323	        self._index_cache_at: float = 0.0
324	
325	        # Per-directory content-signature cache for history-only flows.
326	        # When ``_build_index_fresh`` rebuilds the index, unchanged directories
327	        # (same set of files, same mtimes/sizes) reuse their cached
328	        # :class:`SessionMeta` without re-reading ``_meta.json`` or
329	        # re-extracting the title from the first jsonl line.  The cache is
330	        # keyed by the stringified directory path; each entry maps a
331	        # content-signature tuple to the :class:`SessionMeta` produced from
332	        # that content.  ``invalidate_index_cache`` does *not* clear this
333	        # cache — it self-invalidates via the directory signature.
334	        self._history_meta_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[tuple, SessionMeta]] = {}
335	
336	        # Per-file byte-offset table for incremental reads in :meth:`read_flow`.
337	        # Key: absolute path of the jsonl file (str).
338	        # Value: ``(consumed_lines, byte_offset, mtime, size)`` where
339	        # *consumed_lines* is the count of fully consumed newline-terminated
340	        # lines, *byte_offset* is the file position after the last consumed
341	        # newline, and *mtime*/*size* are the file stat at the time of the last
342	        # read (used to detect truncation / replacement).
343	        #
344	        # When the caller's cursor line-count matches *consumed_lines* and the
345	        # current file size is >= *byte_offset*, only the new bytes past the
346	        # offset are read (seek + incremental parse).  Otherwise (first read,
347	        # cursor rollback, file shrunk) a full read from the start is performed
348	        # and the entry is rebuilt.
349	        self._read_offsets: Dict[str, Tuple[int, int, float, int]] = {}
350	
351	    def invalidate_index_cache(self) -> None:
352	        """Drop the cached index, forcing the next ``build_index`` to rebuild.
353	
354	        Called when a new flow is spawned or a flow status changes, so the
355	        index reflects the new state promptly rather than waiting out the TTL.
356	        """
357	        self._index_cache = None
358	        self._index_cache_at = 0.0
359	
360	    # -- project roots -----------------------------------------------------
361	
362	    def _iter_roots(self) -> List[Path]:
363	        """Return the deduplicated, resolved project roots to enumerate."""
364	        try:
365	            raw = self._provider() or []
366	        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
367	            logger.exception("history: project-roots provider failed")
368	            return []
369	        roots: List[Path] = []
370	        seen: set = set()
371	        for entry in raw:
372	            try:
373	                root = Path(entry).resolve()
374	            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
375	                continue
376	            if root not in seen:
377	                seen.add(root)
378	                roots.append(root)
379	        return roots
380	
381	    # -- index -------------------------------------------------------------
382	
383	    def build_index(self) -> List[SessionMeta]:
384	        """Return :class:`SessionMeta` for every history session, all roots.
385	
386	        Flows are deduplicated by ``flow_id`` (the active ``engine.json`` flow
387	        wins over an archive copy, which wins over a history-only directory)
388	        and sorted by ``updated_at`` descending.
389	
390	        Results are cached for :data:`BUILD_INDEX_TTL` seconds so the daemon
391	        client's per-tick ``_push_history`` call does not trigger a full
392	        directory walk + JSON parse on every fast tick.
393	
394	        Callers that need *live* active-status (e.g. :meth:`read_active_flows`)
395	        must re-check the on-disk ``engine.json`` status because a cached index
396	        may carry stale ``active`` flags for up to the TTL window.
397	        """
398	        now = time.monotonic()
399	        cached = self._index_cache
400	        if cached is not None and (now - self._index_cache_at) < BUILD_INDEX_TTL:
401	            return cached
402	        metas = self._build_index_fresh()
403	        self._index_cache = metas
404	        self._index_cache_at = now
405	        return metas
406	
407	    def _build_index_fresh(self) -> List[SessionMeta]:
408	        """Uncached index build — walks all roots from disk."""
409	        metas: List[SessionMeta] = []
410	        seen: set = set()
411	        for root in self._iter_roots():
412	            try:
413	                self._index_root(root, metas, seen)
414	            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
415	                logger.exception("history: failed to index root %s", root)
416	        metas.sort(key=lambda m: m.updated_at or "", reverse=True)
417	        return metas

1	"""Tests for ``--worktree`` history sidecar merging in the daemon reader.
2	
3	When a ``se3 run --worktree`` flow's per-step history is folded back into the
4	main project by ``se3 merge``'s runtime sync, a colliding per-step ``jsonl``
5	lands as a ``*.jsonl.from-<branch>`` *sidecar* file (Tier A lenient collision
6	policy, see the ``se3 merge`` *Runtime Data Synchronization* requirement). The
7	daemon history reader previously enumerated only ``*.jsonl`` via ``glob``, so
8	those sidecars — and therefore everything after a worktree session's first
9	record — were never read or pushed.
10	
11	These tests pin the fix: :class:`DaemonHistoryReader` now merges the primary
12	file and its sidecars under one logical step id, reads every record with no
13	loss / no duplication / correct ordering, advances its incremental cursor
14	correctly, and parses the step type with the sidecar suffix stripped.
15	"""

The full-read branch currently consumes such a partial line, fails `json.loads`, drops the record, AND advances the cursor past it — so it's never re-read. That's the "first assistant body empty + cursor doesn't advance properly" root cause. Let me check existing read_flow tests for no-trailing-newline expectations.

1330	def _tracking_open_factory():
1331	    """Return ``(patch_fn, get_bytes)`` where ``patch_fn`` is a monkeypatch-
1332	    compatible replacement for ``builtins.open`` that tracks the total bytes
1333	    read via ``.read()`` and ``.readline()`` calls, and ``get_bytes()``
1334	    returns the cumulative count and resets it to zero.
1335	
1336	    Only tracks reads on files under ``tmp_path`` whose suffix is ``.jsonl``.
1337	    """
1338	    import builtins
1339	    import io
1340	
1341	    total_bytes = 0
1342	    _real_open = builtins.open
1343	
1344	    class TrackingFile:
1345	        """Thin wrapper that delegates to the real file but counts reads."""
1346	
1347	        def __init__(self, fh, is_tracked):
1348	            self._fh = fh
1349	            self._tracked = is_tracked
1350	
1351	        def read(self, size=-1):
1352	            data = self._fh.read(size)
1353	            if self._tracked:
1354	                nonlocal total_bytes
1355	                total_bytes += len(data) if isinstance(data, (bytes, str)) else 0
1356	            return data
1357	
1358	        def readline(self, size=-1):
1359	            data = self._fh.readline(size)
1360	            if self._tracked:
1361	                nonlocal total_bytes
1362	                total_bytes += len(data) if isinstance(data, (bytes, str)) else 0
1363	            return data
1364	
1365	        def seek(self, offset, whence=0):
1366	            return self._fh.seek(offset, whence)
1367	
1368	        def tell(self):
1369	            return self._fh.tell()
1370	
1371	        def __enter__(self):
1372	            return self
1373	
1374	        def __exit__(self, *args):
1375	            return self._fh.__exit__(*args)
1376	
1377	        def __getattr__(self, name):
1378	            return getattr(self._fh, name)
1379	
1380	    def tracking_open(file, *args, **kwargs):
1381	        fh = _real_open(file, *args, **kwargs)
1382	        is_tracked = str(file).endswith(".jsonl")
1383	        return TrackingFile(fh, is_tracked)
1384

1386	        nonlocal total_bytes
1387	        val = total_bytes
1388	        total_bytes = 0

def test_full_read_does_not_consume_partial_trailing_line(tmp_path):
    """A FULL read (no cursor) must not consume a half-written final line.

    The worktree / discovery "first assistant body empty, no further records"
    bug: the daemon's first snapshot of a live flow can land while the agent is
    still streaming the latest record (the line has its JSON but no terminating
    ``\\n`` yet).  The full-read path previously consumed that partial line,
    failed ``json.loads``, dropped the record, *and* advanced the cursor past
    it — so the record was lost forever.  The complete records before it must
    read fine, the partial must be left, and once it gains its newline it must
    be picked up incrementally with no loss.
    """
    hist_dir = tmp_path / "se3" / "history" / "f1"
    hist_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    jsonl = hist_dir / "01_discovery_ab.jsonl"
    # First record complete (the user task), then the assistant's first reply
    # written WITHOUT a trailing newline (mid-write).
    user_line = json.dumps(_msg("user", "the task", step_type="discovery"))
    assistant_line = json.dumps(_msg("assistant", "first reply", step_type="discovery"))
    with jsonl.open("wb") as fh:
        fh.write((user_line + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
        fh.write(assistant_line.encode("utf-8"))  # no trailing newline

    reader = _make_reader(tmp_path)
    first = reader.read_flow("f1", project_root=str(tmp_path))
    assert first.mode == HISTORY_MODE_FULL
    # Only the complete first record is read; the partial is left untouched.
    assert [r["message"]["content"] for r in first.records] == ["the task"]
    assert first.cursor == {"01_discovery_ab.jsonl": 1}

    # The writer finishes the assistant line.
    with jsonl.open("ab") as fh:
        fh.write(b"\n")

    second = reader.read_flow(
        "f1", project_root=str(tmp_path), cursor=first.cursor
    )
    assert second.mode == HISTORY_MODE_APPEND
    # The previously-partial record is now read in full — no loss, no truncation.
    assert [r["message"]["content"] for r in second.records] == ["first reply"]
    assert second.cursor == {"01_discovery_ab.jsonl": 2}

    """A cold-cursor full re-read after the partial line completes recovers it.

    Models a daemon restart: the byte-offset table is cold, so the second read
    also takes the full-read branch (with the line now complete).  The record
    must be present and the body non-empty.

def test_read_flow_first_record_nonempty_with_midwrite_sidecar_tail(tmp_path):
    """Symptom B: the first assistant body must read non-empty even when the
    first snapshot lands while the worktree sidecar's tail is mid-write.

    The primary file holds the user task; the worktree sidecar's first
    assistant record is appended WITHOUT its terminating newline (streaming in
    progress).  The full read must surface the user record and leave the
    half-written assistant record for the next round — never consuming it
    half-formed, dropping it, and advancing the cursor past it.
    """
    flow_dir = _flow_dir(tmp_path, "wt-mid")
    primary = flow_dir / "01_discovery_ab12.jsonl"
    sidecar = flow_dir / "01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b"
    _write_jsonl(primary, [_msg("user", "the task")])
    # Sidecar: first assistant record present but NOT newline-terminated.
    partial = json.dumps(_msg("assistant", "first reply body"))
    with sidecar.open("wb") as fh:
        fh.write(partial.encode("utf-8"))

    reader = _make_reader(tmp_path)
    first = reader.read_flow("wt-mid", project_root=str(tmp_path))
    assert first.mode == HISTORY_MODE_FULL
    # The complete primary record reads; the partial sidecar line is held.
    assert [r["message"]["content"] for r in first.records] == ["the task"]
    assert first.cursor["01_discovery_ab12.jsonl"] == 1
    assert first.cursor.get("01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b", 0) == 0

    # The worktree finishes writing the assistant line.
    with sidecar.open("ab") as fh:
        fh.write(b"\n")

    second = reader.read_flow(
        "wt-mid", project_root=str(tmp_path), cursor=first.cursor
    )
    # The first assistant body is now read in full — non-empty, no loss.
    assert [r["message"]["content"] for r in second.records] == ["first reply body"]
    assert all(r["message"]["content"] for r in second.records)
    assert second.cursor["01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b"] == 1

# Group G2: worktree project_root resolution for respond / interject
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _make_reader_root(tmp_path, flow_id, status="RUNNING"):
    """Write a minimal active engine.json so build_index lists *flow_id*."""
    state_dir = tmp_path / "se3" / "state"
    state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (state_dir / "engine.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"flow_id": flow_id, "status": status}), encoding="utf-8"
    )


def test_resolve_flow_root_from_index_returns_attributed_root(tmp_path):
    """``_resolve_flow_root_from_index`` returns the history reader's root.

    This is the SAME ``project_root`` the history reader scopes ``read_flow`` /
    ``read_active_flows`` to, so respond / interject writes line up with the
    history-read path for a ``--worktree`` / discovery session.
    """
    from se3.daemon.history import DaemonHistoryReader

    _make_reader_root(tmp_path, "wt-flow")
    reader = DaemonHistoryReader(project_roots_provider=lambda: [str(tmp_path)])
    client = _make_client(history_provider=reader)

    assert client._resolve_flow_root_from_index("wt-flow") == str(tmp_path)
    # Unknown flow yields empty string (not a crash).
    assert client._resolve_flow_root_from_index("nope") == ""


def test_resolve_flow_root_from_index_without_provider_is_empty():
    """No history provider -> empty string, never an exception."""
    client = _make_client()
    assert client._resolve_flow_root_from_index("any") == ""


def test_interject_falls_back_to_history_index_root(tmp_path):
    """An interjection with no payload root and a snapshot that omits the flow
    resolves the root from the history index and writes the call file there."""
    from se3.daemon.history import DaemonHistoryReader

    _make_reader_root(tmp_path, "wt-flow")

def test_full_read_does_not_consume_partial_trailing_line(tmp_path):

    bug: the daemon's first snapshot of a live flow can land while the agent is

    ``\\n`` yet).  The full-read path previously consumed that partial line,

    jsonl = hist_dir / "01_discovery_ab.jsonl"
    # First record complete (the user task), then the assistant's first reply
    # written WITHOUT a trailing newline (mid-write).
    user_line = json.dumps(_msg("user", "the task", step_type="discovery"))
    assistant_line = json.dumps(_msg("assistant", "first reply", step_type="discovery"))
    with jsonl.open("wb") as fh:

        fh.write(assistant_line.encode("utf-8"))  # no trailing newline

All changes complete and verified. Let me summarize the work.

## Summary

I implemented the daemon-side fixes for **symptom B** (worktree/discovery session: first assistant body empty + no subsequent messages).

**Root cause found (Task 1):** `read_flow`'s full-read branch unconditionally consumed the file's trailing line even when it lacked a terminating newline. For a *live* flow snapshotted while the agent is mid-stream, that last line is truncated JSON — `json.loads` failed, the record was **dropped**, yet `consumed`/the byte offset still advanced past it, so the record was **never re-read** once completed. That's the "first assistant body empty, no further records" symptom. The naïve fix (always drop a no-newline tail) broke terminal step files / sidecars written atomically via `write_text(json.dumps(record))` (valid JSON, no newline) — caught by `test_console_real_daemon_e2e`. The correct fix disambiguates by **parseability**: a parseable tail is a complete atomic write (consumed); an unparseable tail is a mid-write partial (left for the next round).

**Task 2:** `read_active_flows`'s final-flush pass called `read_flow(flow_id, cursor=cursor)` with **no** `project_root`, falling back to an all-roots scan that could resolve the wrong directory (or `None`) for a worktree/discovery flow. It now scopes the flush to the flow's own `project_root` from `build_index`, with the all-roots fallback preserved when a flow is unknown.

**Task 3:** Added `_resolve_flow_root_from_index` (consults the TTL-cached history index — the same `project_root` the history reader uses) and wired it as a fallback in both `_resolve_interject_root` (when the snapshot lags a just-started flow) and `_handle_respond` (when the payload root is empty), keeping respond/interject writes consistent with the history-read root for worktree sessions.

**Task 4:** Added 9 tests across the three test files covering: complete-no-newline tail read, truncated mid-write tail left-and-recovered (full + worktree-sidecar + cold-reread), multi-root final-flush project_root scoping, unknown-flow compat no-op, and the client project_root resolution/interject fallback.

1	"""Historical-session reading for the SE3 daemon.
2	
3	:class:`DaemonHistoryReader` enumerates the ``se3 history`` artifacts of every
4	project root the daemon tracks and turns them into:
5	
6	* a *session index* — one :class:`SessionMeta` per known flow (flow id, task
7	  description, status, timestamps, active flag) — reported to the central
8	  server via :data:`~se3.daemon.protocol.MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` so the web UI can
9	  list historical sessions;
10	* incremental *flow reads* — the per-step ``jsonl`` conversation records of a
11	  single flow (:func:`read_flow`), returned either as a ``full`` snapshot or as
12	  an ``append`` delta keyed off a per-step *line cursor*.
13	
14	Like :class:`~se3.daemon.aggregator.DaemonAggregator`, the reader is a pure
15	reader of the files ``se3 run`` leaves on disk — it never touches a flow's
16	process. The central server is only an in-memory relay; nothing here writes or
17	persists anything server-side.
18	
19	Sources, per project root:
20	
21	* ``se3/state/engine.json`` — the *active* flow (status decides whether it is
22	  still running);
23	* ``se3/state/archive/engine_*.json`` — archived, terminated flows;
24	* ``se3/history/<flow_id>/`` — history-only flows that may have no surviving
25	  ``engine.json`` at all (best-effort metadata is still produced for them).
26	
27	Cursor model
28	------------
29	A *cursor* is a ``{jsonl-filename: line-count-consumed}`` dict. ``jsonl`` files
30	are append-only, so a line count is a stable, monotonic incremental marker. An
31	empty / absent cursor requests a ``full`` snapshot; a populated one requests an
32	``append`` delta. :data:`MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT` bounds a single read so a very
33	large flow cannot OOM the daemon or the wire — the cursor simply advances part
34	way and the remainder is picked up by the next request.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import json
40	import logging
41	import os
42	import re
43	import time
44	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
45	from datetime import datetime
46	from pathlib import Path
47	from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Set, Tuple
48	
49	from .protocol import HISTORY_MODE_APPEND, HISTORY_MODE_FULL

51	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

53	#: Paths already reported as unreadable at WARNING level. The first time a
54	#: corrupt archive / meta file is seen it gets one WARNING; every subsequent
55	#: encounter of the *same* path is logged at DEBUG. This keeps a permanently
56	#: corrupt ``_meta.json`` (re-scanned on every historical enumeration) from
57	#: flooding ``daemon.log`` while preserving first-sight observability. The set
58	#: is naturally bounded by the (small) number of corrupt files on disk.
59	_warned_unreadable_paths: Set[str] = set()
60	
61	
62	def _warn_once_unreadable(path: Path, kind: str) -> None:
63	    """Log an unreadable history file, deduplicated by path.
64	
65	    *kind* is a short noun (``"archive file"`` / ``"meta file"``) spliced into
66	    the message. The first sighting of *path* is a WARNING; repeats are DEBUG.
67	    """
68	    key = str(path)
69	    if key in _warned_unreadable_paths:
70	        logger.debug("history: skipping unreadable %s %s", kind, path)
71	        return
72	    _warned_unreadable_paths.add(key)
73	    logger.warning("history: skipping unreadable %s %s", kind, path)
74

76	#: Hard cap on the number of history records a single :func:`read_flow` call
77	#: returns. When a flow has more new records than this, the read is truncated
78	#: and the returned cursor advances only as far as the truncation point, so the
79	#: caller picks the rest up incrementally on its next request.
80	MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT = 2000
81	
82	#: Flow statuses that mean a flow is no longer running. Anything else on the
83	#: *active* (``engine.json``) source is treated as an in-progress session.
84	_TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset({"completed", "failed"})

87	def _is_active_status(status: str) -> bool:
88	    """Return whether *status* names a still-running (non-terminal) flow.
89	
90	    Anything that is not COMPLETED / FAILED counts as active — INIT, RUNNING,
91	    PAUSED and RECOVERING included — so a flow that pauses (a discovery
92	    clarification, a confirm gate) and is later resumed keeps being read
93	    incrementally rather than dropping out of the active set the moment it
94	    pauses. The comparison is case-insensitive because ``engine.json`` stores
95	    the enum value verbatim (e.g. ``"RUNNING"`` / ``"PAUSED"``).
96	    """
97	    return status.strip().lower() not in _TERMINAL_STATUSES

105	#: *soft* confidence signal by :func:`parse_step_type_from_step_id`; a name
106	#: that follows the file-name convention but is absent here still parses to its
107	#: middle segment, so a future step type drifting out of this set degrades to
108	#: best-effort rather than to a wrong answer.
109	_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES = frozenset(
110	    {
111	        "discovery",
112	        "analyze",
113	        "project_summary",
114	        "plan",
115	        "propose",
116	        "design",
117	        "plan_tasks",
118	        "confirm",

126	        "summarize",

131	def parse_step_type_from_step_id(stem: str) -> str:
132	    """Parse the authoritative step type out of a history jsonl file-name stem.
133	
134	    Real daemon chat-history files are named by the convention
135	    ``NN_<step_type>_<hash>(_Gk)`` (the file-name stem; ``NN`` is a two-digit
136	    sequence number, ``<hash>`` a hexadecimal id, and an optional ``_Gk`` group
137	    suffix is appended for DAG-grouped steps). The raw ``message`` records the
138	    daemon pushes carry *no* ``step_type`` field, so this parser recovers it
139	    deterministically from the stem instead of having the frontend guess.
140	
141	    The middle segment may itself contain underscores (e.g. ``version_analyze``),
142	    so the parser peels the known structural pieces — leading ``NN_`` sequence,
143	    trailing ``_G\\d+`` group suffix, trailing hexadecimal hash — and treats
144	    whatever remains as the step type. Examples::
145	
146	        01_discovery_975607bb      -> "discovery"
147	        13_version_analyze_def456  -> "version_analyze"
148	        05_implement_61605e42_G2   -> "implement"
149	
150	    The result is soft-validated against :data:`_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES`. A name that
151	    clearly follows the convention but whose type is not (yet) known still
152	    returns its parsed middle segment (self-describing, drift-tolerant). An
153	    old / non-conforming name with no sequence prefix and no hash tail (e.g.
154	    the legacy ``commit_summary``) gracefully falls back to the original stem
155	    rather than guessing.
156	
157	    This is a pure function: it never reads disk, has no side effects, and never
158	    raises — any unexpected input yields an empty string.
159	    """
160	    try:
161	        if not isinstance(stem, str):
162	            return ""
163	        original = stem.strip()
164	        if not original:
165	            return ""
166	
167	        # Defensive: if a physical / sidecar file name slipped through (e.g.
168	        # ``01_discovery_ab12.jsonl`` or
169	        # ``01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b``) instead of a logical
170	        # step id, reduce it to the logical id by stripping the ``.jsonl``
171	        # extension and any trailing ``.from-<branch>`` sidecar suffix first, so
172	        # callers that pass a raw name still parse the right step type.
173	        marker = original.find(".jsonl")
174	        if marker >= 0:
175	            original = original[:marker].strip()
176	            if not original:
177	                return ""
178	
179	        s = original
180	
181	        # 1. Strip a leading numeric sequence number ("NN_").
182	        without_seq = re.sub(r"^\d+_", "", s, count=1)
183	        seq_stripped = without_seq != s
184	        s = without_seq
185	
186	        # 2. Strip an optional trailing group suffix ("_G\\d+").
187	        without_group = re.sub(r"_G\d+$", "", s, count=1)
188	        group_stripped = without_group != s
189	        s = without_group
190	
191	        # 3. Strip a trailing hexadecimal hash segment, keeping the middle
192	        #    (which may itself contain underscores, e.g. "version_analyze").
193	        hash_stripped = False
194	        parts = s.split("_")
195	        if (
196	            len(parts) >= 2
197	            and parts[-1]
198	            and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]+", parts[-1])
199	        ):
200	            s = "_".join(parts[:-1])
201	            hash_stripped = True
202	
203	        candidate = s.strip("_")
204	
205	        # Soft-validate against the known step types (authoritative confidence).
206	        if candidate in _KNOWN_STEP_TYPES:
207	            return candidate
208	
209	        # Followed the naming convention (had a sequence / hash / group marker)
210	        # but the type is not in the known set: the parsed middle is still the
211	        # best self-describing answer, so future step types keep working.
212	        if candidate and (seq_stripped or hash_stripped or group_stripped):
213	            return candidate
214	
215	        # Old / non-conforming name (no NN prefix, no hash, e.g.
216	        # "commit_summary"): fall back to the original stem rather than guess.
217	        return original
218	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - parser must never raise

304	class DaemonHistoryReader:
305	    """Builds a history index and serves incremental per-flow conversation reads."""
306	
307	    def __init__(self, project_roots_provider: ProjectRootsProvider) -> None:
308	        """Create a reader.
309	
310	        Args:
311	            project_roots_provider: Zero-arg callable returning the project
312	                roots whose ``se3/history`` should be enumerated. Wiring this
313	                to the aggregator's ``project_roots`` keeps the history view in
314	                lock-step with the rest of the daemon's tracked roots.
315	        """
316	        self._provider = project_roots_provider
317	        # TTL cache for :meth:`build_index`.  The daemon client's push loop
318	        # calls ``build_index`` every fast tick (1 s); on a large history tree
319	        # the full directory walk + JSON parse is expensive enough to saturate
320	        # thread-pool workers.  Caching for a conservative window collapses
321	        # repeated identical rebuilds into one.
322	        self._index_cache: Optional[List[SessionMeta]] = None
323	        self._index_cache_at: float = 0.0
324	
325	        # Per-directory content-signature cache for history-only flows.
326	        # When ``_build_index_fresh`` rebuilds the index, unchanged directories
327	        # (same set of files, same mtimes/sizes) reuse their cached
328	        # :class:`SessionMeta` without re-reading ``_meta.json`` or
329	        # re-extracting the title from the first jsonl line.  The cache is
330	        # keyed by the stringified directory path; each entry maps a
331	        # content-signature tuple to the :class:`SessionMeta` produced from
332	        # that content.  ``invalidate_index_cache`` does *not* clear this
333	        # cache — it self-invalidates via the directory signature.
334	        self._history_meta_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[tuple, SessionMeta]] = {}
335	
336	        # Per-file byte-offset table for incremental reads in :meth:`read_flow`.
337	        # Key: absolute path of the jsonl file (str).
338	        # Value: ``(consumed_lines, byte_offset, mtime, size)`` where
339	        # *consumed_lines* is the count of fully consumed newline-terminated
340	        # lines, *byte_offset* is the file position after the last consumed
341	        # newline, and *mtime*/*size* are the file stat at the time of the last
342	        # read (used to detect truncation / replacement).
343	        #
344	        # When the caller's cursor line-count matches *consumed_lines* and the
345	        # current file size is >= *byte_offset*, only the new bytes past the
346	        # offset are read (seek + incremental parse).  Otherwise (first read,
347	        # cursor rollback, file shrunk) a full read from the start is performed
348	        # and the entry is rebuilt.
349	        self._read_offsets: Dict[str, Tuple[int, int, float, int]] = {}
350	
351	    def invalidate_index_cache(self) -> None:
352	        """Drop the cached index, forcing the next ``build_index`` to rebuild.
353	
354	        Called when a new flow is spawned or a flow status changes, so the
355	        index reflects the new state promptly rather than waiting out the TTL.
356	        """
357	        self._index_cache = None
358	        self._index_cache_at = 0.0
359	
360	    # -- project roots -----------------------------------------------------
361	
362	    def _iter_roots(self) -> List[Path]:
363	        """Return the deduplicated, resolved project roots to enumerate."""
364	        try:
365	            raw = self._provider() or []
366	        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
367	            logger.exception("history: project-roots provider failed")
368	            return []
369	        roots: List[Path] = []
370	        seen: set = set()
371	        for entry in raw:
372	            try:
373	                root = Path(entry).resolve()
374	            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
375	                continue
376	            if root not in seen:
377	                seen.add(root)
378	                roots.append(root)
379	        return roots
380	
381	    # -- index -------------------------------------------------------------
382	
383	    def build_index(self) -> List[SessionMeta]:
384	        """Return :class:`SessionMeta` for every history session, all roots.
385	
386	        Flows are deduplicated by ``flow_id`` (the active ``engine.json`` flow
387	        wins over an archive copy, which wins over a history-only directory)
388	        and sorted by ``updated_at`` descending.
389	
390	        Results are cached for :data:`BUILD_INDEX_TTL` seconds so the daemon
391	        client's per-tick ``_push_history`` call does not trigger a full
392	        directory walk + JSON parse on every fast tick.
393	
394	        Callers that need *live* active-status (e.g. :meth:`read_active_flows`)
395	        must re-check the on-disk ``engine.json`` status because a cached index
396	        may carry stale ``active`` flags for up to the TTL window.
397	        """
398	        now = time.monotonic()
399	        cached = self._index_cache
400	        if cached is not None and (now - self._index_cache_at) < BUILD_INDEX_TTL:
401	            return cached
402	        metas = self._build_index_fresh()
403	        self._index_cache = metas
404	        self._index_cache_at = now
405	        return metas
406	
407	    def _build_index_fresh(self) -> List[SessionMeta]:
408	        """Uncached index build — walks all roots from disk."""
409	        metas: List[SessionMeta] = []
410	        seen: set = set()
411	        for root in self._iter_roots():
412	            try:
413	                self._index_root(root, metas, seen)
414	            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
415	                logger.exception("history: failed to index root %s", root)
416	        metas.sort(key=lambda m: m.updated_at or "", reverse=True)
417	        return metas
418	
419	    @staticmethod
420	    def _is_still_active(meta: SessionMeta) -> bool:
421	        """Re-check whether *meta*'s flow is still active on disk.
422	
423	        The :meth:`build_index` cache may carry stale ``active`` flags for up
424	        to :data:`BUILD_INDEX_TTL` seconds.  This lightweight re-check reads
425	        only the single ``engine.json`` for the flow's project root (a
426	        ``stat`` + small JSON parse), which is dramatically cheaper than the
427	        full index rebuild it replaces.
428	        """
429	        if not meta.active:
430	            return False
431	        if meta.source != "active":
432	            return False
433	        engine_json = Path(meta.project_root) / "se3" / "state" / "engine.json"
434	        data = _read_json(engine_json)
435	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
436	            return False
437	        # Confirm the engine.json still describes *this* flow.  Without this
438	        # check, if flow F1 completed and a different flow F2 is now the
439	        # active engine.json flow (status RUNNING), _is_still_active(F1_meta)
440	        # would read F2's RUNNING status and incorrectly return True — keeping
441	        # the stale F1 meta in the active set and missing F2 entirely.
442	        if str(data.get("flow_id") or "") != meta.flow_id:
443	            return False
444	        status = str(data.get("status") or "")
445	        return _is_active_status(status)
446	
447	    def _index_root(
448	        self, root: Path, metas: List[SessionMeta], seen: set
449	    ) -> None:
450	        """Append the sessions found under one project *root* into *metas*."""
451	        state_dir = root / "se3" / "state"
452	
453	        # 1. Active flow from engine.json.
454	        data = _read_json(state_dir / "engine.json")
455	        if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("flow_id"):
456	            flow_id = str(data["flow_id"])
457	            if flow_id not in seen:
458	                seen.add(flow_id)
459	                metas.append(self._meta_from_engine(root, data, source="active"))
460	
461	        # 2. Archived flows.
462	        archive_dir = state_dir / "archive"
463	        if archive_dir.is_dir():
464	            for archive_file in sorted(archive_dir.glob("engine_*.json")):
465	                adata = _read_json(archive_file)
466	                if not isinstance(adata, dict):
467	                    continue
468	                flow_id = str(adata.get("flow_id") or "")
469	                if not flow_id or flow_id in seen:
470	                    continue
471	                seen.add(flow_id)
472	                metas.append(
473	                    self._meta_from_engine(
474	                        root,
475	                        adata,
476	                        source="archived",
477	                        fallback_mtime=_safe_mtime(archive_file),
478	                    )
479	                )
480	
481	        # 3. History-only flows (may have no engine.json at all).
482	        history_root = root / "se3" / "history"
483	        if history_root.is_dir():
484	            for flow_dir in sorted(history_root.iterdir()):
485	                if not flow_dir.is_dir():
486	                    continue
487	                flow_id = flow_dir.name
488	                if flow_id in seen:
489	                    continue
490	                seen.add(flow_id)
491	                metas.append(self._meta_from_history(root, flow_dir))
492	
493	    def _meta_from_engine(
494	        self,
495	        root: Path,
496	        data: Dict[str, Any],
497	        *,
498	        source: str,
499	        fallback_mtime: Optional[float] = None,
500	    ) -> SessionMeta:
501	        """Build a :class:`SessionMeta` from an ``engine.json``-shaped dict."""
502	        status = str(data.get("status") or "unknown")
503	        active = source == "active" and _is_active_status(status)
504	        updated = str(data.get("updated_at") or "")
505	        if not updated and fallback_mtime:
506	            updated = datetime.fromtimestamp(fallback_mtime).isoformat()
507	        flow_id = str(data.get("flow_id"))
508	        return SessionMeta(
509	            flow_id=flow_id,
510	            project_root=str(root),
511	            task_description=_clip(str(data.get("task_description") or "")),
512	            task_type=str(data.get("task_type") or ""),
513	            status=status,
514	            created_at=str(data.get("created_at") or ""),
515	            updated_at=updated,
516	            active=active,
517	            source=source,
518	            step_count=_count_jsonl(root / "se3" / "history" / flow_id),
519	            # A flow is only meaningfully "waiting for lock" while it is the live
520	            # active flow; an archived/terminal snapshot is never queued. Reading
521	            # only on the active source also keeps a stale True out of history.
522	            waiting_for_lock=bool(active and data.get("waiting_for_lock", False)),
523	        )
